name: Dimethylglycine (DMG)

lead: DMG is a natural metabolite of betaine and choline, found in beans and liver, and sold as a supplement for endurance, oxygen use and immune support. Users take it hoping for quicker recovery and more consistent training, which they tie to a better physique.

It sits in the methyl-donor pathway, produced from betaine and converted to sarcosine, and has acted at the NMDA receptor glycine site in mice. Trials in autism showed little difference from placebo and a Cochrane review found no benefit in mitochondrial disease; no athletic trials are cited.

paras: People take it as capsules or sublingual tablets, often alongside other recovery or endurance supplements, and judge it by how training and recovery feel over a few weeks.
In concentrated form it is labelled harmful if swallowed, and the rat oral LD50 is above 650 mg/kg. Human safety data are limited in the sources reviewed.

forums.title: DMG - pop it or poop it?

angle.text: DMG is sold for endurance, oxygen use and immune support, and users take it for quicker recovery and more consistent training. Trials in autism and mitochondrial disease have been small or null, and none look at appearance or training outcomes.

lead: Dimethylglycine (DMG) is a derivative of the amino acid glycine with two methyl groups on the nitrogen. It forms during the breakdown of betaine (trimethylglycine) and choline, and occurs in foods such as beans and liver [1][2]. It was once called vitamin B16, though it is not considered a true vitamin because deficiency causes no ill effects [1].

As a supplement it has been proposed as an athletic performance enhancer, immunostimulant, and treatment for autism, epilepsy and mitochondrial disease [1]. Wikipedia reports that trials in autism spectrum disorders showed little to no difference from placebo and that a Cochrane review found no evidence of benefit in mitochondrial disease [1]. Evidence for athletic or appearance outcomes is not provided in these sources. In looksmaxxing and recovery circles it is discussed as an endurance and oxygen-use aid.

paras: DMG forms white crystals melting near 178 to 182 degrees C and is sold as the free amino acid or hydrochloride [1]. In the body it is produced when betaine donates a methyl group to homocysteine, a step catalysed by betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase, and is further demethylated in mitochondria to sarcosine as part of one-carbon metabolism [2][3][4]. A 2016 mouse study found DMG acted as an agonist at the glycine site of the NMDA receptor [1].

Reference text describes historical use among Russian athletes and cosmonauts for endurance and oxygen utilisation [2]; the claim comes from a non-peer-reviewed source and is not backed by trial data in these sources.

Wikipedia reports that studies in autism spectrum disorders showed little to no difference between DMG and placebo, and that a Cochrane review found no evidence it helps mitochondrial disease [1]. No trial of DMG for athletic performance, recovery or appearance is cited in the available sources.
DMG carries a GHS warning for being harmful if swallowed, and the oral LD50 in rats is above 650 mg/kg [1].
